summary: Round 4, and there is still no line of logic to mutate: the only src/main edit is SubscriptionEvent's field javadoc, the only test edit is a class javadoc and one .as() description string, and every assertion predicate is byte-identical -- nothing weakened. I re-measured rather than accepted the two claims this commit rests on. (1) The falsifiability claim in the test javadoc holds exactly as stated: forcing decode to discard the parsed range (byteStart=byteLen=RANGE_ABSENT after the two uvarints) reds 3 of 281 format cases -- aRangeStartingAtBYTEZEROIsNotMistakenForABSENT and aV3EventSurvivesAROUNDTrip in SubscriptionEventGrantTest, aV3DIRECTEventWithARangeMatchesItsGoldenBytes in GoldenSubscriptionEventTest -- and :format:test is green with the mutation reverted. (2) The unasked-for correction to M5.66's premise is TRUE against source, so the row is not scoped on a false premise: SegmentKey.headerLenOf plus SegmentFormat.PREAMBLE_BYTES make [0, PREAMBLE+headerLen) computable from the event's own segmentKey; SegmentPublisher.headerRangeEndInclusive:147 computes it and SegmentPublisherTest:144-150 fetches getRange(key, 0, end) and reads runCount back out of it, so that range is not merely expressible but exercised today. codecAndFlags is per run in the DIRECTORY (SegmentFormat:17-18, RunEntry:19) and the DATA frame is [u32 uncompressedLen][u32 crc32c][records] with no codec id, so the codec objection does rule out the slice-only form only. SegmentReader.open checks footer magic before building the directory and read(RunEntry) indexes the whole buffer absolutely, so what is missing genuinely is one new entry point, not a wire change. Two majors, both on M5.66's criterion 2, and they point the same way: the third wording EXCLUDES the two-request bounded read the row exists to authorise and ADMITS a slice-only reader that ignores the codec. Plus the retired 'no range is expressible' claim surviving in three places this commit did not sweep, one of them the test javadoc named as a handoff site.

findings.location: docs/internal/product/backlog.md:126 (M5.66 criterion 2, 'at one run of 1,600, strictly FEWER BYTES and NO MORE REQUESTS than the whole-object GET')
findings.title: Criterion 2's relation at the favourable share is unsatisfiable by the two-request bounded read the same cell establishes -- arm 1 cannot be discharged as written
findings.failure_scenario: The whole-object baseline is ONE request. The bounded read this row specifies is header range then slice -- TWO. The cell says so itself, twice: 'directory-then-slice is TWO requests where a whole-object GET is one, so this row trades a request for bandwidth and must say at which node share that trade wins', and 'this row's own "two requests versus one" framing is true only at K = 1'. So at the one-run share the intended design makes 2 requests against the baseline's 1, and 'NO MORE REQUESTS than the whole-object GET' reds it. At the ~400 share it is worse (1 header + N slices). Arm 1 is therefore undischargeable at BOTH shares by any directory-then-slice implementation, which is the only implementation the row, ADR-0044's Decision (b) table and SubscriptionEvent's new javadoc all describe. Two things survive the criterion instead: (i) arm 2 -- take the fields off the wire, a format change under non-negotiable 8 that reverses ADR-0044's decision, chosen not on the measurement criterion 1 demands but on a wording artifact; (ii) a single prefix GET [0, byteStart+byteLen) fed to a new reader that skips the footer check -- 1 request, fewer bytes at an early run -- which ADR-0044:89 lists as NOT expressible precisely because SegmentReader.open refuses it, and which at a late run fetches nearly the whole object anyway. ⚠️ This is a REGRESSION introduced by the fix: round 3's minor proposed 'at the favourable share strictly fewer bytes and AT MOST 2 REQUESTS', and the landed wording is 'NO MORE REQUESTS than the whole-object GET', which is at most 1. The repair is to restore the budget form and keep the 401-killer where it belongs: at one run of 1,600, strictly fewer bytes and AT MOST TWO requests; at ADR-0042's ~400-of-1,600 share, NO MORE BYTES AND NO MORE REQUESTS than the whole-object path's 8 MiB and 1 request per (node, segment). That kills the 'directory GET plus one ranged GET per run, always on' implementation the clause was written for, without forbidding the design the row was created to make possible.

findings.location: docs/internal/product/backlog.md:126 (M5.66 criterion 2, 'with the codec reachable from what was fetched'), against format/src/main/java/binjava/format/SegmentWriter.java:109 and SegmentReader.java:134-150
findings.title: 'Codec reachable from what was fetched' is satisfiable by assertion: a slice-only reader that never fetches the directory passes every clause of criterion 2 today
findings.failure_scenario: Surviving implementation, satisfying all four criteria: decodeRun(byte[] slice, long byteStart, long byteLen, int recordCount) -- a reader fed ONLY the bytes of [byteStart, byteStart+byteLen), which needs nothing from the directory, because recordCount is carried on the SubscriptionEvent itself and SegmentReader.read never consults codecAndFlags at all. Gate it on the crossover: bounded below, whole-object above. At one run of 1,600 that is ONE ranged GET of ~5.2 KiB -- strictly fewer bytes, no more requests than the whole-object GET, and it even satisfies the criterion-2 relation my other finding says the two-request form cannot. At the ~400 share it falls back and is no worse on either count. The coordinates drive it, a bounded read exists, criterion 3 then 'corrects' SubscriptionEvent's javadoc to say a reader consumes them, and the fields look earned. The implementer discharges 'codec reachable' by observing what is true in the tree: SegmentWriter:109 writes CODEC_NONE unconditionally and no reader reads the field back, so the codec IS trivially reachable today. It stops being reachable the moment any writer sets a non-zero codec -- and at that point every direct consumer below the crossover feeds compressed bytes to the record cursor and either throws a block checksum mismatch or decodes garbage, on a path no test covers. NAMED MUTATION THAT SURVIVES: write a non-zero codecAndFlags into a run's directory entry and change nothing else -- no case in this row's criteria reds, because nothing requires the fetched-and-decoded run to have a codec that had to be read from somewhere. The repair is one clause: the case decodes a run whose directory entry declares a NON-ZERO codecAndFlags, and the reader's behaviour on it is asserted (honoured, or refused by name). That forces the directory into what was fetched and is the only wording that makes 'reachable' cost anything.

findings.location: format/src/test/java/binjava/format/SubscriptionEventGrantTest.java:23-26, with docs/internal/product/decisions/0044-no-production-fetcher-in-m5-and-the-coordinates-stay.md:163-165 and :223-224, against the same file's :80-99
findings.title: 'No range is expressible' survives in three sites this commit did not sweep, including the test javadoc named as a handoff for security.md rule 3, while the same commit retires the claim as too strong
findings.failure_scenario: ADR-0044:80-99 states the claim is 'TOO STRONG' and tables two ranges that ARE expressible today, one of which I verified is computed and fetched in the tree (SegmentPublisher:147, SegmentPublisherTest:144-150). The correction reached the research banners, the backlog row and SubscriptionEvent's field javadoc. It did NOT reach: (a) SubscriptionEventGrantTest:23-26 -- 'the grant is scoped to one key and to NO range, because no range is expressible ... There is nothing for a signature to cover'; (b) ADR-0044:163-165, Decision (c) -- 'no range is expressible FOR THE REASONS UNDER (b)', citing for the claim the very section that refutes it 80 lines above; (c) ADR-0044:223-224, alternative (b2) -- 'no range is expressible'. The last sentence of (a) is flatly false as written: the header range is nameable from the key and signable today; what is not nameable is [0, objectLen), which is the one range the consumer path's whole-object read would need. The consequence is the one criterion 4 exists to prevent: M5.66's owner is sent to this test javadoc as one of three handoff sites for security.md rule 3's range half, reads 'there is nothing for a signature to cover', and closes the clause by declining it on a capability statement the same commit proves wrong. This is the one-of-two-places defect ADR-0044 itself names five times and that round 1 of this task blocked on -- here inside one file, with the pointer running into its own refutation. The fix is to replace the reason, not the conclusion, at all three sites: the grant carries no range because the only fetch the consumer path makes is a whole-object read and [0, objectLen) is not nameable -- and to add the sweep-table row saying so, since 'Corrected' is currently recorded against a site that still carries the retired claim.

findings.location: docs/internal/product/backlog.md:126 (M5.66 criterion 1, 'THE CODE'S THRESHOLD IS DERIVED FROM THE RECORDED NUMBER')
findings.title: The derivedFrom half of the round-3 fix landed and the boundary-case half did not; the recorded crossover is still pinned only to a 400-wide window
findings.failure_scenario: Round 3's minor asked for two things: the threshold IS the recorded constant, AND cases at crossover-1 and crossover+1 deriving their input from it. The first landed (the derivedFrom shape, which exists and takes the per-GB price as an explicit argument -- FetchPolicyConfig:103,119 -- so criterion 1's 'CostTable holds no per-byte price' is accurate). The second did not. Criterion 2 exercises exactly two shares, and they constrain the threshold only to the open interval [1, 400): K=1 must take the bounded path, K~400 must be no worse than whole-object, which forces fallback. NAMED MUTATION THAT SURVIVES: measure and record a crossover of K = 40, then let the derivation produce 300 (a wrong bandwidth price, a wrong constant, a units slip) -- both asserted shares stay green, and every node holding 40 to 300 runs runs the policy the record says loses. Nothing reads the recorded number and the computed one together. Restoring the dropped half -- one case at the crossover and one at crossover+1, taking opposite paths, with their input derived from the same constant -- is what makes the measurement bind. Minor, because the window is bounded at both ends and the consequence is a cost inefficiency rather than a correctness or request-rate break.

findings.title: The sweep table is split in two by its own 'this table is the single enumeration' paragraph, and the seven rows after it do not render as a table
findings.failure_scenario: Rows :296-302 follow a paragraph, with no header and no delimiter row, so under GFM they are not table rows at all -- they render as a paragraph of literal pipe characters. A reader of the rendered record sees a twelve-row table, then a closing note that reads exactly like a closing note ('THIS TABLE IS THE SINGLE ENUMERATION'), then a block of raw text. The seven sites below the break include the format/.../SubscriptionEventGrantTest.java row and the doc 04 2c banner row that round 1 called blocking. M5.66's criterion 3 makes this table THE enumeration and points at it rather than copying it, which is the right rung -- so the artifact being visually truncated at the exact line a reader would stop is worth one edit: move the paragraph above the table's header row, or below its last row. Minor because the rows remain greppable and diffable in source, which is where the criterion's check will actually be run.
